title: How Does a QR Code Actually Work?
sources: Japan Patent Office, 'QR Code: development story' (jpo.go.jp/e/news/koho/innovation/01_qrcode_e.html) and IEEE Spectrum, 'How a Board Game and Skyscrapers Inspired the Development of the QR Code': invented in 1994 by Masahiro Hara's team at Denso Wave (Japan) to track automotive parts; the three position-detection (finder) squares let a scanner find the code and its orientation from any angle

QR error correction (t.ly 'QR Codes Correction Levels', qrcode-tiger 'QR Code Error Correction', Linkly): Reed-Solomon error correction; level H can restore about 30% of the code's data, so a damaged or partly covered code still scans
ISO/IEC 18004 summary (Wikipedia 'QR code'): data is stored as dark and light modules read as binary 1 and 0 in a 2D grid

US FTC consumer alert (Dec 2023, via PYMNTS / Entrepreneur) and 2026 parking-lot QR warnings (WDAM): scammers cover legitimate QR codes with their own stickers that lead to phishing sites; check the URL before opening it

lines.text: How does a QR code turn little black squares into a website?
lines.caps: HOW *DOES | A *QR CODE | *TURN | LITTLE BLACK *SQUARES | INTO A *WEBSITE?

lines.text: Well, every square is one bit:
black means one, and white means zero,
and your camera reads them like a secret message.
Those three big squares in the corners?
They tell your phone which way is up,
so it scans from almost any angle.
so with up to thirty percent torn off, it still works.
lines.caps: *SO WITH | UP TO *30% | *TORN OFF | IT STILL *WORKS

lines.text: It was invented in Japan in nineteen ninety-four, to track car parts.
lines.caps: IT WAS *INVENTED | IN *JAPAN | IN *1994 | TO *TRACK | *CAR PARTS

lines.text: a QR code is just a link,
and scammers stick fake ones over real ones.
So always check the link before you tap.
